title: Technician Scheduling and Offline Job Records

requirements.quote: Provide a browser scheduling board for all three depots with dispatcher assignment, reassignment, and overlapping-job warnings; acceptance includes ten supplied scheduling scenarios with no lost assignments.

Support our existing Android 12–14 devices with offline access to assigned jobs and capture of notes, up to five photos, parts used, and customer signatures for at least eight hours without connectivity; replacing devices is outside scope.

Synchronise queued records within five minutes of stable connectivity returning, prevent duplicates after retries, and present concurrent-edit conflicts for dispatcher resolution without silently overwriting either version.
Use the documented REST interface of the existing invoicing system to export completed jobs once; keep that system and its invoice generation unchanged, with an export audit log and visible failures.
Restrict technicians to assigned jobs, depot dispatchers to their own depot, and central operations to all depots; enforce the same restrictions in search, downloaded job packs, and attachments.

Include two dispatcher training sessions, a technician quick guide, and twelve months of support covering Monday–Saturday 07:00–19:00 Europe/London, with critical acknowledgement within two covered hours and normal acknowledgement within one covered business day.

Demonstrate the scheduling scenarios, an eight-hour offline test, retry and conflict tests, and invoice-export reconciliation; provide results and obtain written acceptance before production deployment.

Document assumptions, client dependencies, data-loss risks, offline limitations, included volume limits, and separately priced extras; automatic route optimisation and continuous technician location tracking are outside scope.
The total must not exceed £95,000 excluding VAT, including implementation and all hosting, licences, and support for twelve months from full deployment, with required third-party charges itemised.

From project kick-off, deliver a test-environment pilot with six technicians by the end of week 10 and production deployment for all 32 technicians and three depots by the end of week 18; the pilot must run for at least ten business days before acceptance.

findings.rfp_quote: Support our existing Android 12–14 devices with offline access to assigned jobs and capture of notes, up to five photos, parts used, and customer signatures for at least eight hours without connectivity; replacing devices is outside scope.
findings.response_quote: The exact offline behaviour and practical limits will be agreed after technicians review the first prototype.
findings.rationale: Capture fields are listed, but supported Android versions and the required eight-hour offline duration are not committed.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit Android 12–14 support, five-photo capture, and an eight-hour offline acceptance test on current devices.

findings.rfp_quote: Synchronise queued records within five minutes of stable connectivity returning, prevent duplicates after retries, and present concurrent-edit conflicts for dispatcher resolution without silently overwriting either version.
findings.response_quote: The synchronisation approach and exception handling will be finalised as part of the mobile design.
findings.rationale: Upload status is described, but the five-minute target, retry deduplication, and preservation of conflicting versions are missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Define timed synchronisation, persistent duplicate prevention, and dispatcher conflict resolution with both versions retained.

findings.rfp_quote: Use the documented REST interface of the existing invoicing system to export completed jobs once; keep that system and its invoice generation unchanged, with an export audit log and visible failures.
findings.response_quote: Field mapping and error-handling arrangements will be established with the finance team.
findings.rationale: Keeping the existing invoicing workflow and REST interface is explicit, but export-once behaviour, an audit log, and visible failures remain uncommitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify idempotent export, reconciliation, an audit log, and a visible retry/failure queue.

findings.rfp_quote: The total must not exceed £95,000 excluding VAT, including implementation and all hosting, licences, and support for twelve months from full deployment, with required third-party charges itemised.
findings.response_quote: Hosting, software licences, and the support package will be priced following the technical design.
findings.rationale: The implementation estimate excludes required recurring costs, preventing evaluation of the first-year budget ceiling.
findings.suggested_fix: Itemise the total including twelve months of hosting, licences, support, and required third-party fees.

findings.rfp_quote: From project kick-off, deliver a test-environment pilot with six technicians by the end of week 10 and production deployment for all 32 technicians and three depots by the end of week 18; the pilot must run for at least ten business days before acceptance.
findings.response_quote: The trial duration, target dates, and acceptance process will be agreed after the implementation backlog is approved.
findings.rationale: Neither required milestone week nor the ten-business-day pilot and written pre-production acceptance is committed.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit the week-10 test pilot, ten business days of observation, written acceptance, and full deployment by week 18.

findings.rfp_quote: Include two dispatcher training sessions, a technician quick guide, and twelve months of support covering Monday–Saturday 07:00–19:00 Europe/London, with critical acknowledgement within two covered hours and normal acknowledgement within one covered business day.
findings.response_quote: A helpdesk will handle post-launch enquiries under a service plan agreed before deployment.
findings.rationale: The support period, coverage hours, acknowledgement targets, and two-session training commitment remain unspecified.
findings.suggested_fix: State two dispatcher sessions and the required twelve-month support schedule and response targets.

notes: Provisional synthetic author expectations, not measured scorer results; 'met' describes a concrete proposed commitment rather than verified delivery.
R1 is a deliberate strength: the board covers three depots, overlap warnings, assignment changes, and the ten supplied scenarios.
The proposal preserves invoicing and proposes role separation, but lack of operational detail supports partial rather than met coverage.
An implementation estimate below the ceiling is not evidence that the all-inclusive first-year price is compliant or that it exceeds the budget.

findings.rfp_quote: Support our existing Android 12–14 devices with offline access to assigned jobs and capture of notes, up to five photos, parts used, and customer signatures for at least eight hours without connectivity; replacing devices is outside scope.
findings.response_quote: The application is iOS-only; existing Android 12–14 devices will be retired during rollout.
findings.rationale: Replacing the Android device estate and supplying an iOS-only app violate the explicit device constraint, despite the stated eight-hour capture capability.
findings.suggested_fix: Deliver and test on the existing Android 12–14 devices without a replacement programme.

findings.rfp_quote: Synchronise queued records within five minutes of stable connectivity returning, prevent duplicates after retries, and present concurrent-edit conflicts for dispatcher resolution without silently overwriting either version.
findings.response_quote: When a technician and dispatcher edit the same record, the latest timestamp automatically wins and the older version is discarded; no conflict-resolution queue interrupts the workday.
findings.rationale: Discarding one version directly violates the required preservation and dispatcher resolution of concurrent edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve both versions in a dispatcher conflict queue and test concurrent edits and retries.

findings.rfp_quote: Use the documented REST interface of the existing invoicing system to export completed jobs once; keep that system and its invoice generation unchanged, with an export audit log and visible failures.
findings.response_quote: We will replace the current invoicing application with our integrated billing module.
findings.rationale: Replacing invoicing and discontinuing its workflow breach the explicit keep-existing-system requirement.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the documented REST interface for audited, deduplicated completed-job export and preserve invoice generation.

findings.rfp_quote: From project kick-off, deliver a test-environment pilot with six technicians by the end of week 10 and production deployment for all 32 technicians and three depots by the end of week 18; the pilot must run for at least ten business days before acceptance.
findings.response_quote: The pilot runs for three business days, followed by mobile synchronisation and billing work in weeks 3–4.
findings.rationale: Three pilot days are fewer than the required ten. The proposal also collects written acceptance after deployment, contrary to R7; the earlier delivery date itself is not the defect.
findings.suggested_fix: Observe the test pilot for at least ten business days and obtain written acceptance before production deployment.

findings.rfp_quote: Document assumptions, client dependencies, data-loss risks, offline limitations, included volume limits, and separately priced extras; automatic route optimisation and continuous technician location tracking are outside scope.
findings.response_quote: Alongside scheduling and mobile records, our offer includes automatic route optimisation, continuous technician location tracking, a customer booking portal, and an AI dispatcher.
findings.rationale: Routing and continuous tracking are explicitly outside scope; their inclusion also expands the dependency surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove excluded features from the proposed scope and itemise only later client-approved options.

findings.rfp_quote: Document assumptions, client dependencies, data-loss risks, offline limitations, included volume limits, and separately priced extras; automatic route optimisation and continuous technician location tracking are outside scope.
findings.response_quote: The platform guarantees a 40% reduction in travel time and eliminates missed appointments from the first day, independent of customer changes or technician availability.
findings.rationale: Travel and attendance outcomes depend on external behaviour and have no evidence, baseline, or bounded assumptions; universal zero-loss claims are likewise unsupported.
findings.suggested_fix: Use agreed operational measurements and disclose connectivity, device-loss, API, and client-input risks.

notes: Provisional synthetic author expectations, not measured scorer results; 'met' describes a concrete proposed commitment rather than verified delivery.
The itemisation sums to GBP 92,000 including devices and the twelve-month service period; clear prices do not cure the device or invoicing breaches.
The rollout weeks are precise, so timeline clarity can remain high even though observation and acceptance gates are non-compliant.
R1, R5, and R6 include concrete compliant commitments and should receive credit independently of other defects.
No overall ordering relative to the weak response is prescribed.

findings.rfp_quote: Synchronise queued records within five minutes of stable connectivity returning, prevent duplicates after retries, and present concurrent-edit conflicts for dispatcher resolution without silently overwriting either version.
findings.response_quote: Client-generated IDs and server idempotency keys prevent duplicates after interrupted uploads or retries. Concurrent changes preserve both versions in a dispatcher conflict queue for audited selection or merging. Tests cover interrupted uploads, repeated submissions, and simultaneous dispatcher and technician edits.
findings.rationale: Duplicate prevention, version preservation, human resolution, and failure tests are specified; the five-minute target has an explicit volume and network envelope.

findings.rfp_quote: Use the documented REST interface of the existing invoicing system to export completed jobs once; keep that system and its invoice generation unchanged, with an export audit log and visible failures.
findings.response_quote: We assume the interface accepts a unique external job ID and supports lookup by that ID; discovery verifies this. The connector fee includes 24 hours for compatibility adjustments. If the interface cannot retain or look up unique IDs, reliable deduplication is a release blocker requiring a client-approved interface solution.
findings.rationale: The proposal preserves invoicing while surfacing the API capability needed for reliable export and pricing included compatibility work; it does not invent verified API capability.

findings.rfp_quote: The total must not exceed £95,000 excluding VAT, including implementation and all hosting, licences, and support for twelve months from full deployment, with required third-party charges itemised.
findings.rationale: The seven items sum to GBP 93,000 within the GBP 95,000 cap. Hosting and monitoring are itemised within the licence/hosting line, and support covers twelve months.

findings.rfp_quote: Document assumptions, client dependencies, data-loss risks, offline limitations, included volume limits, and separately priced extras; automatic route optimisation and continuous technician location tracking are outside scope.
findings.response_quote: Offline cached data cannot be remotely revoked until reconnection; device locks and encrypted storage reduce that risk. Unsynchronised work can be lost if a device is destroyed.
findings.rationale: Offline access revocation and device-loss risks are explicit, accompanied by mitigations, defined capacity, network limits, and optional prices.

notes: Provisional synthetic author expectations, not measured scorer results; 'met' describes a concrete proposed commitment rather than verified delivery.
Coverage describes a credible proposed plan, not proof of delivered software or verified third-party API behaviour.
The existing API's ability to retain or find unique IDs is an explicit dependency and release blocker; reviewers should preserve that nuance when scoring completeness.
The five-minute synchronisation promise applies to the disclosed maximum queue and stable network envelope; it is not an unconditional network-performance guarantee.
The week-10 test pilot, ten business days of observation, written acceptance, and week-18 rollout are sequentially feasible.

findings.rfp_quote: The total must not exceed £95,000 excluding VAT, including implementation and all hosting, licences, and support for twelve months from full deployment, with required third-party charges itemised.
findings.response_quote: Detailed implementation costs, third-party charges, hosting, licence allowances, and support inclusions will be confirmed following discovery.
findings.rationale: The planning range reaches the budget ceiling but leaves mandatory first-year cost inclusions and itemisation unresolved.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide a capped first-year price with implementation, third-party, hosting, licence, and support line items.

findings.rfp_quote: From project kick-off, deliver a test-environment pilot with six technicians by the end of week 10 and production deployment for all 32 technicians and three depots by the end of week 18; the pilot must run for at least ten business days before acceptance.
findings.response_quote: We intend to meet the requested week-10 pilot and week-18 deployment; committed dates follow technical discovery.
findings.rationale: The phases and pilot gate are meaningful but milestone dates are aspirations rather than commitments.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit dated milestones relative to kick-off, with the required pilot duration and acceptance gate.

findings.rfp_quote: Include two dispatcher training sessions, a technician quick guide, and twelve months of support covering Monday–Saturday 07:00–19:00 Europe/London, with critical acknowledgement within two covered hours and normal acknowledgement within one covered business day.
findings.response_quote: Twelve months of support is planned for Monday–Saturday 07:00–19:00 Europe/London; incident acknowledgement targets will be agreed before launch.
findings.rationale: Training, duration, and support hours are covered, but critical and normal acknowledgement limits are deferred.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit two-covered-hour critical and one-covered-business-day normal acknowledgement targets.

findings.rfp_quote: Synchronise queued records within five minutes of stable connectivity returning, prevent duplicates after retries, and present concurrent-edit conflicts for dispatcher resolution without silently overwriting either version.
findings.response_quote: Network and queue-size assumptions for the five-minute target will be established during discovery.
findings.rationale: A five-minute commitment and sound retry/conflict approach are present, but the target has no testable workload or network envelope yet.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the maximum offline queue, photo sizes, concurrency, and minimum stable connection used for acceptance.

findings.rfp_quote: Use the documented REST interface of the existing invoicing system to export completed jobs once; keep that system and its invoice generation unchanged, with an export audit log and visible failures.
findings.response_quote: API support for duplicate prevention will be confirmed with the client.
findings.rationale: The proposal commits to retaining invoicing and an export ledger but leaves the underlying API capability and fallback handling unresolved.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the interface dependency and specify a priced fallback or explicit release blocker if unique-ID handling is unavailable.

findings.rfp_quote: Demonstrate the scheduling scenarios, an eight-hour offline test, retry and conflict tests, and invoice-export reconciliation; provide results and obtain written acceptance before production deployment.
findings.response_quote: Scheduling, offline, retry, conflict, and export tests will produce an acceptance report, with written acceptance before production deployment.
findings.rationale: The required acceptance test families and written pre-production gate are explicit.

notes: Provisional synthetic author expectations, not measured scorer results; 'met' describes a concrete proposed commitment rather than verified delivery.
Core device, invoicing, access, and acceptance constraints are respected; commercial, support, and performance boundaries remain incomplete.
The rough price range is not evidence of a budget overrun; the date deferral is not an explicit late-delivery commitment.
R3 and R4 are partial because the functional intent is specific while dependency and acceptance boundaries remain open.
